title: Uncertain spam signals should not hide customer mail
summary: When agents add spam protection to a customer-facing mailbox, they may treat authentication failures, sender reputation hints, or broad content keywords as enough evidence to auto-quarantine messages. For unknown external senders, those signals are uncertain; hiding mail can lose legitimate customer contact. Keep uncertain detections visible as labels, shadow scores, or audit events until a stricter business policy and verification gate exists.
ai_value: Prevents agents from converting detection logic into message-hiding behavior before proving that the signal is definitive enough for the mailbox's customer-communication risk.

contexts: Applications that ingest or display customer-facing email in a mailbox, CRM, helpdesk, marketplace, or support workflow
Spam or abuse classifiers based on SPF, DKIM, DMARC, sender domain, content keywords, user reports, or external reputation signals
Rule engines or settings tables that can label, move, hide, quarantine, retain, or delete mail

trigger_signals.description: A new spam feature can move, hide, quarantine, or delete messages from unknown external senders based on authentication failure or missing authentication alone.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat this as a customer-mail visibility gate, not just a classifier implementation detail.

trigger_signals.description: A database setting or admin mode says quarantine, but code and API gates do not independently hold or reject quarantine for uncertain signals.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Storage shape must not be enough to activate message-hiding behavior.

trigger_signals.description: Trusted-domain or own-domain configuration is editable or data-driven and could silently widen self-spoof quarantine beyond the explicitly launched domain set.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Prove a launch allowlist or equivalent policy boundary prevents accidental scope expansion.

negative_signals.description: The action only adds a visible label, score, audit entry, or shadow-mode assessment and does not move, hide, suppress, retain, or delete the message.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Detection-only work can usually proceed with ordinary validation because customer visibility is preserved.

negative_signals.description: The message is a definitive own-domain self-spoof under a reviewed allowlist and failed/missing authentication condition, or the exact sender was manually blocked by an authorized user action.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Some narrow cases can be strong enough for quarantine when tests prove the boundary and no broader customer-mail rule is activated.

negative_signals.description: A reviewed policy explicitly authorizes the exact sender class, signal class, mailbox, retention behavior, and user-visible recovery path for quarantine or deletion.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The trap targets accidental or premature quarantine, not execution of a precise approved policy.

common_wrong_assumptions: Authentication failure from an external domain always means the message is spam.
If a setting row says quarantine, the feature is safe to activate without code-level launch holds.
Broad content words in subject or body are enough to move customer mail out of the inbox.
Adding a spam folder is reversible enough that no owner or business policy gate is needed.
A trusted-domain table can double as the production allowlist for self-spoof quarantine without a separate launch boundary.

first_checks.check: Enumerate every code path that can move, hide, quarantine, suppress, retain, or delete mail, including rule execution, API settings, scheduled jobs, and manual actions.
first_checks.why: Spam classifiers often have multiple effect paths; a safe label-only path can be bypassed by a settings or worker path.

first_checks.check: Add negative fixtures for unknown external senders with failed, missing, or misaligned authentication and spammy-looking content.
first_checks.why: These fixtures should remain visible in the inbox or normal mail list unless a reviewed policy says otherwise.

first_checks.check: Add positive fixtures only for definitive cases, such as own-domain self-spoof constrained by an explicit allowlist, and exact-sender manual blocks.
first_checks.why: Positive tests should prove the narrow live behavior without broadening uncertain external-domain quarantine.

first_checks.check: Test that database settings, admin API updates, and rule-engine execution all reject or hold general quarantine while policy is pending.
first_checks.why: A database mode can become an accidental feature flag if enforcement exists in only one layer.

decision_rules.condition: A signal is uncertain and the sender may be a legitimate external customer.
decision_rules.then: Keep the message visible and record the assessment as a label, score, audit event, or shadow decision instead of moving or hiding it.

decision_rules.condition: A setting, API, or rule action would enable general quarantine, retention, or deletion before policy approval.
decision_rules.then: Stop before activation and ask for the exact sender class, mailbox scope, retention/delete semantics, recovery path, and monitoring requirement.

decision_rules.condition: The case is definitive own-domain self-spoof and an explicit launch allowlist plus failed/missing authentication are both proven by tests.
decision_rules.then: Allow the narrow quarantine path while keeping external-domain and non-allowlisted-domain cases label-only or shadow.

decision_rules.condition: The behavior is a user-initiated exact-sender block or manual spam action.
decision_rules.then: Confirm the action is exact-sender scoped, auditable, and reversible through the product's normal user/admin controls before relying on it as a live path.

do_not: Do not auto-quarantine unknown external-domain mail solely because SPF, DKIM, or DMARC failed or is missing.
Do not turn a database quarantine mode into live behavior unless API and rule execution layers enforce the same policy boundary.
Do not let trusted-domain rows silently expand own-domain self-spoof quarantine beyond an explicit launch allowlist.
Do not infer deletion, retention, or permanent suppression semantics from a quarantine feature request.
Do not hide customer-visible mail with broad keyword classifiers unless the exact policy and recovery path have been reviewed.
Do not use this signal-confidence record to decide retention or provider deletion semantics; cross-check mailbox-folder-move-is-not-retention-or-provider-delete for count-evidence effect separation.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Before enabling any mail-hiding action, classify each signal as definitive or uncertain, prove uncertain cases remain visible, and gate quarantine/deletion semantics through the exact reviewed policy.

risk.notes: This trap protects customer communications and potential data-loss/visibility boundaries. It does not authorize changing production mail routing, retention, deletion, security, or permission behavior without the applicable reviewed or human gate.

sources.supports: A de-identified production mail-spam implementation found that database quarantine mode and trusted-domain data could have widened live quarantine unless code/API launch holds and allowlist filtering were enforced. The safe result kept uncertain external-domain spam label-only/shadow while allowing only narrow definitive self-spoof and manual exact-sender block paths.
